The basket before the bicycle ride

Shared bank: be | because | careful | child | choose | heavy | help | two | we | with

There ____1____ several bicycles beside the garden gate on Saturday. My cousins had come for a short supervised ride with our parents. We checked ____2____ bags before leaving, because nothing should hang loosely near the wheels.

Dad attached a basket to one bicycle and checked it ____3____. This was our ____4____ ride together; the first had been along a shorter path near home. Two younger ____5____ would join for only the first part before returning with an adult.

We ____6____ the riverside route after looking at the weather and path information. One bag was much ____7____ than the others because it held everyone's water. Dad moved the bottles between suitable bags instead of expecting one person to carry everything.

We stopped near the bridge ____8____ a group of walkers was passing. Waiting was easier than trying to push through a narrow space. I held my bicycle ____9____ both hands and watched the river while the others passed.

Back home, we hoped ____10____ tidy the equipment before lunch. The ride had not been long, but it had included many small arrangements that made travelling together easier. My younger cousin asked whether the next route could pass the bakery. Dad said we could discuss it after eating the lunch already waiting inside.

Our classmates ____1____ short messages for a postcard display. Some described holidays, while others showed familiar streets near home. Everyone placed ____2____ name on the back so the teacher could return the card afterwards.

One pupil had drawn a market ____5____, using bright colours and tiny details. Another had ____6____ an afternoon making a simple black-and-white view of a station. Neither had used a photograph as the finished postcard.

We enjoyed ____7____ the places through one another's accounts. A postcard could not show a whole city, but it could preserve a particular view. We thanked everyone ____8____ explaining why they had chosen their picture.

My brother, who is two years ____9____ than I am, came to see the wall after school. He asked whether he could draw a card for it too. The teacher found space beside the other work. We ____10____ to add new cards next term, keeping a copy of the first display before taking it down. The wall had become a collection of choices and stories, not just a row of tourist landmarks.

On the ____4____ visit, after eleven earlier short checks, we compared our notes. There were noticeable ____5____ between morning and afternoon use. We did not merge every observation into a single claim about a typical day.

We used dated sheets ____6____ of relying on a shared memory of what had happened. Some notes had been ____7____ in a hurry, so their authors checked the wording before we used them in the report.

That decision did not solve every issue, and we listed questions for a later review rather than declare the project permanently finished.
